payload.task_text:
You are working for an event catering company that has been hired to plan a corporate team building event menu for 30 people. Your task is to design a complete catering plan and get client approval.

Use the HowToCook recipe database to browse recipes across different categories. Select at least 8 dishes to create a full catering menu with appetizers, main courses, and at least one dessert or soup. Choose recipes that would work well for a corporate team building setting serving 30 people.

Create an Excel workbook called Catering_Plan.xlsx in your workspace with two sheets. The first sheet must be named Menu and include the columns Dish_Name, Category (use values like Appetizer, Main_Course, Soup, or Dessert), Servings_For_30 (the number of servings needed to feed the 30 guests, which is approximately 30 — one serving per guest — scaled up from the recipe's default serving count), Prep_Time_Minutes (estimated preparation time as a number), and Estimated_Cost_USD (estimated cost in US dollars as a number, estimate $3-8 per serving for most dishes). Write all numeric values (Servings_For_30, Prep_Time_Minutes, Estimated_Cost_USD, and any quantities) as literal numbers, not Excel formulas. The Menu sheet should have at least 8 data rows. The second sheet must be named Ingredients and include the columns Dish_Name, Ingredient, Quantity_For_30_People, and Unit.

Create a Word document called Catering_Proposal.docx in your workspace. Include an executive summary describing the event and your catering approach, a menu overview section listing all selected dishes with brief descriptions, and a preparation timeline section describing when each category of dish will be prepared on the event day.

Create a Google Form called "Menu Approval Survey" with questions to collect client feedback on the proposed menu. Include at least three questions: one asking the client to rate overall menu satisfaction, one asking which dishes they want to confirm or remove, and one asking for any special dietary requirements or additional notes.

Send an email to client@corporate.com with subject "Catering Proposal for Team Building Event" that summarizes the proposed menu and mentions that the Excel plan, Word proposal, and feedback form have been prepared.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, complete it directly in the main agent; do not dispatch sub-agents. Make one bounded category-discovery pass, select exactly eight suitable dishes covering appetizers, main courses, and at least one soup or dessert, and retrieve those eight recipe details with native-parallel calls. Freeze one eight-dish table and reuse it everywhere. Create `Catering_Plan.xlsx`, `Catering_Proposal.docx`, and the Form `Menu Approval Survey` as independent output branches. The workbook must use the exact two sheets and headers, literal numeric values, `Servings_For_30` values scaled to approximately 30, positive costs, and ingredient rows referencing the same dish names. Build the Word document with one bulk structured body containing the exact title, Executive Summary, Menu Overview, and Preparation Timeline and mentioning at least four exact selected dish names. Create the Form exactly once with these three explicit questions: `Rate the overall menu satisfaction from 1 to 5`; `Which dishes should we confirm or remove?`; and `List any special dietary requirements or additional notes`. Verify each deliverable once, then send exactly one email to `client@corporate.com` with subject `Catering Proposal for Team Building Event`.

You are planning a multi-step task for an event catering company. Please decompose the following task into ordered subtasks and produce a detailed plan.

TASK DESCRIPTION:
Design a complete catering plan for a corporate team building event menu for 30 people, using the HowToCook recipe database (accessible via mcp__howtocook__* tools). Then get client approval.

Requirements:
1. Browse the HowToCook recipe database across categories (categories include: 水产, 早餐, 调料, 甜品, 饮品, 荤菜, 半成品加工, 汤, 主食, 素菜). Select AT LEAST 8 dishes to create a full catering menu with appetizers, main courses, and at least one dessert or soup. Choose recipes suitable for a corporate team building setting serving 30 people.

2. Create Excel workbook Catering_Plan.xlsx in the workspace directory /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-howtocook-event-catering-excel-word/workspace with TWO sheets:
   - Sheet 1 named "Menu" with columns: Dish_Name, Category (values like Appetizer, Main_Course, Soup, or Dessert), Servings_For_30 (number of servings needed to feed 30 guests, approximately 30 — one serving per guest — scaled up from recipe's default serving count), Prep_Time_Minutes (estimated prep time as number), Estimated_Cost_USD (estimated cost in USD as number, $3-8 per serving for most dishes). All numeric values must be literal numbers, NOT Excel formulas. At least 8 data rows.
   - Sheet 2 named "Ingredients" with columns: Dish_Name, Ingredient, Quantity_For_30_People, Unit.

3. Create Word document Catering_Proposal.docx in the workspace with:
   - Executive summary describing the event and catering approach
   - Menu overview section listing all selected dishes with brief descriptions
   - Preparation timeline section describing when each category of dish will be prepared on the event day

4. Create a Google Form called "Menu Approval Survey" with at least 3 questions: one rating overall menu satisfaction, one asking which dishes to confirm or remove, one asking for special dietary requirements or additional notes.

5. Send an email to client@corporate.com with subject "Catering Proposal for Team Building Event" summarizing the proposed menu and mentioning that the Excel plan, Word proposal, and feedback form have been prepared.

TOOLS AVAILABLE (task-scoped):
- mcp__howtocook__* : recipe database (getAllRecipes, getRecipeById, getRecipesByCategory, recommendMeals, whatToEat)
- mcp__excel__* : Excel workbook operations (create_workbook, create_worksheet, write_data_to_excel, rename_worksheet, etc.)
- mcp__word__* : Word document operations (create_document, add_heading, add_paragraph, add_table, etc.)
- mcp__google_forms__* : Google Forms operations (create_form, add_multiple_choice_question, add_checkbox_question, add_text_question)
- mcp__emails__* : Email operations (send_email)
- mcp__filesystem__* and mcp__local__python_execute : file system and python execution in the workspace

For each subtask, specify:
- Dispatch decision: self (main agent), explore, or coder
- Whether independent (parallelizable) or dependent on another subtask's output
- Key acceptance criteria

Consider: which recipe categories best map to Appetizer/Main_Course/Soup/Dessert (the HowToCook categories are Chinese cooking categories - e.g., 素菜=vegetable dishes could be appetizers, 荤菜=meat dishes could be main courses, 汤=soup, 甜品=dessert, 主食=staple food); how to get recipe details (ingredients with quantities, default serving counts) to scale to 30 people; the order of operations (recipe selection first, then Excel, then Word, then Form, then Email — the email should reference all other deliverables so it must come last, though form creation can be parallel with documents).

Return a concise ordered plan with clear subtask definitions, dispatch decisions, dependencies, and acceptance criteria.

Use add_heading with level 1 for main section titles and level 2 for subsections. Keep paragraphs concise.

DOCUMENT TITLE (use add_heading level 0 or a title paragraph): Catering Proposal — Corporate Team Building Event
Subtitle paragraph: Prepared for: Corporate Client | 30 Guests | Event Catering Services

SECTION 1 — Executive Summary (heading level 1)
Content paragraphs:
- "This proposal presents a complete catering plan for a corporate team building event serving 30 guests. Our approach combines crowd-pleasing flavors with practical, scalable preparation: a balanced buffet menu of appetizers, main courses, soup, and desserts selected from the HowToCook recipe library."
- "Every dish was chosen for its broad appeal, manageable preparation, and ability to be scaled reliably to 30 servings. The menu balances light starters, hearty mains, a warming soup, and two desserts to satisfy a wide range of tastes. Estimated cost ranges from $3 to $8 per serving per dish, with a total estimated budget of approximately $1,170 (about $39 per guest)."
- "All supporting materials — the detailed Catering_Plan.xlsx workbook with menu and scaled ingredient quantities, this written proposal, and a Menu Approval Survey for client feedback — have been prepared to streamline approval and finalize event-day execution."

SECTION 2 — Menu Overview (heading level 1)
Intro paragraph: "The following nine dishes form the proposed menu. Each was selected for suitability in a team building setting: easy to serve buffet-style, visually appealing, and broadly liked."

List each dish as a heading level 2 followed by a one-sentence description paragraph:
1. Cold Cucumber Salad (凉拌黄瓜) — Appetizer: Crisp smashed cucumbers tossed in a garlicky soy-vinegar dressing with sesame oil; a light and refreshing starter.
2. Wood Ear Mushroom Salad (凉拌木耳) — Appetizer: Tender wood ear mushrooms dressed with a tangy chili-garlic vinaigrette; crunchy, healthy, and palate-cleansing.
3. Boiled Shrimp (白灼虾) — Main Course: Fresh shrimp gently poached and served with a soy-vinegar dipping sauce; simple, elegant, and high in protein.
4. Kung Pao Chicken (宫保鸡丁) — Main Course: Classic Sichuan stir-fry of chicken, roasted peanuts, and dried chilies in a sweet-sour savory sauce.
5. Cola Chicken Wings (可乐鸡翅) — Main Course: Glossy, caramelized chicken wings braised in cola and soy; a sweet-savory crowd favorite.
6. Sweet and Sour Pork (糖醋里脊) — Main Course: Crispy golden pork tenderloin tossed in a tangy sweet-and-sour sauce; universally loved.
7. Corn Pork Rib Soup (玉米排骨汤) — Soup: Slow-simmered pork rib broth with sweet corn and carrot; warming, comforting, and easy to serve in cups.
8. Yogurt Panna Cotta (酸奶意式奶冻) — Dessert: Silky chilled Italian panna cotta lightened with plain yogurt; a creamy, refreshing finish.
9. Fried Milk (炸鲜奶) — Dessert: Crispy golden-fried milk custard bites; a playful and indulgent sweet ending.

SECTION 3 — Preparation Timeline (heading level 1)
Intro paragraph: "The event-day kitchen schedule staggers preparation so every dish is served fresh and at the right temperature."
Subsections (heading level 2) with paragraph content:
- Early Morning (6:00 – 8:00): "Start the Corn Pork Rib Soup, the longest-cooking item: blanch the ribs, begin the slow simmer with corn and carrot. Soak the dried wood ear mushrooms. Prepare the Yogurt Panna Cotta mixture, portion into cups, and refrigerate to set."
- Mid-Morning (8:00 – 10:00): "Marinate the chicken for Kung Pao Chicken and the pork for Sweet and Sour Pork. Prep all vegetables. Braise the Cola Chicken Wings and allow them to glaze. Prepare the Fried Milk custard and chill it until firm."
- Late Morning (10:00 – 12:00): "Assemble the cold appetizers (Cold Cucumber Salad and Wood Ear Mushroom Salad). Poach the Boiled Shrimp. Fry the Sweet and Sour Pork and the Fried Milk. Finish seasoning the soup."
- Service (12:00 – 13:00): "Set up the buffet: appetizers and chilled desserts first, then hot mains and soup in warming trays. Keep the Fried Milk and Boiled Shrimp freshly replenished."
- Afternoon (13:00 – 14:00): "Clear and clean service stations, conduct post-event quality checks, and collect client feedback through the Menu Approval Survey."
